result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly call the plan a feature tour and move discovery to the start. B is stronger on cutting: it puts the dashboard, reporting, integrations and mobile app on reserve, ranks the problems, and requires a dated next step with an owner. A gives more concrete trade scenarios and prep, but it keeps more of the tour. Neither answer covers what each of the three attendees is watching for or how to check during the demo that it is landing. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B says plainly that the plan is a feature tour and that this is the main risk. It builds the demo around two or three workflows matched to their business, such as fitting a same-day emergency into a full schedule, rerouting around it and texting the customer an ETA, and it saves 10 minutes for questions and a dated next step. A is sharper about cutting sections (it names dashboard, reporting, integrations and the mobile app as reserve material), but it demos individual features rather than their situations from start to finish. Neither answer really covers what each of the three attendees is watching for.
